title: Expose customer-receipt allocation evidence in order reconciliation workflows
description: Extend existing Sales Order and ERP-046 customer order/receipt reconciliation workflows with read-only allocation evidence from ERP-053. Keep ordered, shipped and receipt-reference evidence distinct and do not calculate or claim an accounts-receivable balance, settlement result, due date, aging bucket or Customer credit decision. Do not infer links, mutate source records, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Sales Order detail exposes active allocated customer-receipt evidence, allocation count and unallocated or unavailable context using only canonical persisted ERP-053 allocation rows.
Sales Order lists expose a bounded receipt-evidence summary without issuing a database query per row.

The ERP-046 customer order/receipt reconciliation workflow displays recorded receipt-reference evidence alongside ordered and shipment evidence while keeping each evidence class in separately labeled fields.
Customer and currency mismatches in historical evidence are displayed as invalid or unavailable and are never silently converted, merged or reassigned.
Voided allocation evidence is excluded from active totals but remains inspectable through an explicit historical status or detail view.
Missing receipt allocation evidence is shown as none or unknown as appropriate and is never converted into unpaid, paid, overdue, settled or outstanding status.

The UI and documentation state that receipt allocations are operational reference evidence, not confirmation of bank settlement, an accounts-receivable ledger, a legal Customer statement, payment authorization or credit decision.
The workflow is read-only and does not change Sales Orders, shipment records, receipt documents, Customer credit state, inventory, invoices, commissions, expenses or tax records.
Queries are bounded or paged, avoid per-row database access and reuse ERP-032, ERP-046 and ERP-053 authoritative semantics rather than implementing a second reconciliation engine.
Existing orders and reports with no explicit allocation rows remain readable without request-time or production backfill.

Unit/integration tests cover no evidence, partial and multiple allocations, void history, mismatched historical evidence, multiple Customers and currencies, bounded queries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Open a Sales Order with partial shipment and customer-receipt allocation evidence and verify ordered, shipped and receipt-reference values remain separately labeled and match their source records.
Inspect an order with voided, mismatched or missing receipt evidence and verify it is not presented as paid, settled, outstanding or overdue and that no source record changes.

human_gate.reason: Read-only presentation of repository receipt-reference evidence. No real receipt, production mutation, settlement, credit decision, deployment or release is authorized.
